reason: The hypothesis combines the well-known effect of grain boundaries on oxidation (P1, P2) with the specific defect structure of an additively manufactured alloy and proposes a post-manufacturing heat treatment to test the mechanism. However, the core idea—that high defect density accelerates diffusion, leading to non-protective oxide scales, internal oxidation, and failure—is a direct restatement of findings and proposed mechanisms from P1, P2, P9, P14, P22, and P29. The intervention (heat treatment to reduce defects) is the same approach studied in P1, P2, P16, P18, and P28. The application to a new alloy composition (Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3) is a minor change without a new mechanistic justification, and the hypothesis does not resolve any conflict or gap in the cited literature.
